unmapped_findings: S1000 impact behaviour (instrumented Charpy): total absorbed energy 29.2 J comprises crack initiation energy and crack propagation energy; crack propagation energy is 9.87 J and the load-displacement displacement is 4.55 mm (lowest of the three conditions).
S1000 austenite composition measured by EDS (Table 2), wt.%: Mn 20.97 ± 0.34, Al 9.30 ± 0.02, Ni 2.04 ± 0.26, Cr 3.24 ± 0.78, C 1.17 ± 0.13, Fe Bal.
Cube-austenite/κ-carbide orientation relationship for S1000: [011]γ // [011]κ (κ-carbide co-gridded with austenite, additional faint superlattice diffraction spots in SAED).

Cr7C3 on the grain boundaries of S1000 causes preferential crack nucleation at grain boundaries (aggregated micropores), and cracks generally follow the random high-angle boundaries; the special boundaries in S1000 have limited effect on changing crack propagation or deflection, giving intergranular fracture characteristics.

S1000 impact fracture surface shows quasi-cleavage planes with slip bands, microcracks and microvoids; the shear zone area of S1000 is the smallest of the three conditions (larger shear zone correlates with better toughness).

The paper reports sample density of the alloy as 6.78 g/cm³ (drainage method, ~14 % lower than pure iron 7.87 g/cm³) for the base ingot, applicable to the studied alloy rather than to a specific heat-treatment state.
